title: Nose gear
object: Steerable oleo-pneumatic nose landing gear of a four-seat high-wing light aircraft, in section on the aircraft's centre line, with its steering in plan and its wheel in front section
idea: An air spring with an oil damper: a strut that carries the nose, soaks up the landing and steers
summary: The nose wheel touches down at 0.9 m/s: the piston tube slides into the cylinder, squeezing the air charge (p·V^1.1) and forcing oil up through an orifice that a tapered metering pin closes down as the stroke deepens, so the force grows with the stroke and the speed squared. A snubber ring slows the rebound and the strut settles at 95 mm under 17 % of the aircraft's weight. The pedals steer the wheel through bungee springs against a shimmy damper; on lift-off the strut extends and the centering cams straighten the wheel.
usedFor: Pilot and maintenance training: what the nose strut's 45 psi does, why it is serviced extended, what the cams and shimmy damper are for
Engineering courses: oleo-pneumatic struts, polytropic air springs, orifice damping, metering pins
A software-concept explainer: a fail-safe default (the cams centre the wheel whenever the strut is unloaded) and compliant coupling (bungees that give instead of fighting)
